newsitem.title: UK: Employment rises in UK small, medium firms - survey.
newsitem.headline: Employment rises in UK small, medium firms - survey.

text.p: Employment in Britain's small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) has risen significantly over the last four months for the first time in a year, according to a survey released on Monday.

The survey, by the Confederation of British Industry (CBI) and chartered accountants Pannell Kerr Forster, showed business confidence among SMEs rose for the first time since April 1995 and total new orders and output were up.

"Our survey shows that small and medium-sized enterprises have staged a recovery since the summer, with employment growing and a return in business confidence," said Tony Bonner, chairman of the CBI's SME Council.

Over the past four months 27 percent of SMEs reported an increase in employment and 21 percent a fall, giving a positive balance of six percent of firms reporting increases compared to a balance of minus two percent in July.
Employment over the next four months was expected to grow by a positive balance of four percent.
The rise in employment for SMEs contrasted with the overall picture for British manufacturing, which showed a small reduction in employment with a sharp fall expected over the next four months.

SMEs also reported business optimism had risen for the first time since July last year and was at the highest rate since April 1995, with a positive balance of 10 percent saying they were more optimistic than four months ago.
Total orders received by SMEs had risen a little more quickly over the past four months, while export orders fell slightly.
The survey showed manufacturing output for SMEs had picked up and was expected to rise more strongly, particularly for medium sized firms.
However, SME's unit costs had fallen slightly for the first time since January 1994 and over the next quarter no overall change was expected.

All categories of stocks remained virtually unchanged over the past four months, contrary to expectations of small reductions. Little change in stock levels was anticipated over the four months ahead.
